title: Optimization of TiO2/SiO2/Glass Stack
scientific_hypothesis: Placing the higher refractive index material (TiO2) adjacent to the air incident medium and the lower index material (SiO2) adjacent to the glass substrate will yield a lower arithmetic mean reflectance over the 450-700 nm band compared to the reverse order, given the specific thickness constraints of 40-160 nm.
design_principle: Impedance matching via stepped refractive index profile (Air -> High -> Low -> Substrate) to minimize Fresnel reflections at interfaces, optimized for broadband performance within geometric constraints.
proposed_topology: Air | TiO2 (Layer 1) | SiO2 (Layer 2) | Glass Substrate. Total finite layers: 2.
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (s-pol, normal incidence) from 450 nm to 700 nm
manufacturing_considerations: Layer thicknesses must strictly remain between 40 nm and 160 nm
theory_basis: Thin-film interference theory suggests that a high-low index sequence can provide better broadband matching for high-index substrates than low-high, depending on the specific index values and wavelength range.
Quarter-wave approximation provides an initial guess, but broadband minimization requires deviation from single-wavelength quarter-wave conditions.
expected_advantages: Potentially smoother spectral response due to the gradual index transition from Air (1.0) to TiO2 (2.40) to SiO2 (1.46) to Glass (1.52).
TiO2 as the first layer may offer stronger phase control for the short wavelengths in the band.
known_risks: The large index jump from Air to TiO2 might create a strong reflection peak that the second layer cannot fully suppress within the thickness limits.
The optimal solution might lie on the boundary of the thickness constraints (40 or 160 nm), limiting further improvement.
execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic TMM optimization for a planar stack: Incident Medium Air (n=1.0), Layer 1 TiO2 (n=2.40, lossless), Layer 2 SiO2 (n=1.46, lossless), Substrate Glass (n=1.52, lossless). Illumination: Normal incidence (0 deg), s-polarization. Wavelength range: 450 nm to 700 nm, sampled every 5 nm. Objective: Minimize the arithmetic mean of power reflectance across the sampled wavelengths. Design variables: Thickness of Layer 1 and Layer 2, both bounded between 40 nm and 160 nm. Optimization settings: Maximum 64 solver evaluations, random seed 17. Output the optimal thicknesses, the full reflectance spectrum, the calculated mean reflectance, and the best target score. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization s. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm; achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the 450 nm to 700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm; exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2.
